**Review candidate, not a released model dataset.** This CGIAR [Sustainable Farming Science Program](https://www.cgiar.org/cgiar-research-portfolio-2025-2030/sustainable-farming) collaboration involves IITA and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT. Cedric Ngakou developed the ERA-to-Carob transformation and merge; Namita Joshi contributed integration, reporting and fixes and leads climate integration.

### Two deliverables, one repository and one CGSpace record

See [package metadata and credits](audit/packages.json), the [shared publication metadata](audit/publication.json) and [release/publication decisions](audit/RELEASE.md). ### ERA data version

The current build uses the **issue #94 date-only successor of the May 2025 ERA bundle**, labelled `2026-11-23-issue94` and published on 24 November 2026. Its JSON retains the same Majestic Hippo and Industrious Elephant source cohorts, row order and non-date values, while correcting date decoding and recovering lost dates. The vocabulary (`2025-05-12`) and compiled comparison Parquet are unchanged. [Current archive and SHA-256](audit/inputs.json).

The June replay still uses the original **12 May 2025** bundle through [historical pins](audit/inputs-historical.json), in a separate cache. The proposed software version `0.1` is distinct from either input version.

### Build and inspect the candidate

PRs [#2](https://github.com/CGIAR-AgWise/era-carob/pull/2) and [#3](https://github.com/CGIAR-AgWise/era-carob/pull/3) are merged. Start from current main and record its exact commit; for repeatable review, check out the agreed commit. From a terminal with Git, curl, Python 3 and R installed:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/CGIAR-AgWise/era-carob.git
cd era-carob
git switch main
git pull --ff-only
git rev-parse HEAD
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("dplyr","tidyr","stringr","jsonlite","data.table","digest"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
export SF001_INPUTS="$PWD/downloaded_data/sf001-issue94"
python3 audit/prepare.py "$SF001_INPUTS"
Rscript audit/build.R
Rscript -e 'd <- as.data.frame(readRDS(file.path(Sys.getenv("SF001_INPUTS"),"sf001-review.rds"))); print(table(d$source)); print(head(d[c("source","source_row","dataset_id","crop_raw","crop","yield")]))'
```

Preparation verifies the two archives and retains the corrected source’s date audit and holds. The build checks prepared-file hashes and carries all 900 row/field holds in the local RDS metadata. The build resolves crops against the supplied ERA vocabulary, checks each retained row against its source and writes the review dataset locally. For the June replay, exact snapshot checks and workbook generation, follow the [reproduction instructions](audit/RELEASE.md#reproduce).

### What the pinned comparison measures

Each retained ERA row has a distinct ordinal in the source archive's `Data.Out` outcome table. Each Carob row is one record in the June agronomy wide table. These units differ. A dataset ID counts a source study in ERA or a dataset in Carob. A Carob trial is a nonblank **(dataset_id, trial_id)** pair; study, location or row number cannot substitute for a trial ID in ERA.

| Pinned candidate | ERA | Carob |
|:---|---:|---:|
| Input rows (ERA source outcomes / Carob wide records) | `r fmt(s$era_source)` | `r fmt(s$carob_rows)` |
| Retained rows | `r fmt(cur$wide_rows[cur$source=="era"])` | `r fmt(cur$wide_rows[cur$source=="carob"])` |
| Distinct source study / dataset IDs | `r fmt(cur$datasets[cur$source=="era"])` | `r fmt(cur$datasets[cur$source=="carob"])` |
| Identifiable trials | Unknown (no trial IDs) | `r fmt(s$trials)` |
| Crop yield rows with numeric kg/ha | `r fmt(cur$numeric_yield_rows[cur$source=="era"])` | `r fmt(cur$numeric_yield_rows[cur$source=="carob"])` |

Together these sources contribute **`r fmt(sum(cur$wide_rows))` stacked rows**; this is not a count of independent observations or trials. Carob trial IDs are populated on `r fmt(cur$identified_trial_rows[cur$source=="carob"])` rows. Publication-DOI matching gives **`r s$doi_edges` dataset links for `r s$doi_studies` ERA studies** in the historical comparison; for example, DK0071 links to three Carob datasets. A shared article flags possible overlap, not duplicate measurements. Do not subtract 21 rows or discard all data from these studies. [Study links](report/audit/publication_links.csv)

| Crop counting rule | ERA only | Both | Carob only |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| June replay: distinct nonblank crop strings, trimmed and lowercased | `r s$raw[1]` | `r s$raw[2]` | `r s$raw[3]` |
| June replay: resolved ERA product identities only | `r s$resolved[1]` | `r s$resolved[2]` | `r s$resolved[3]` |
| Corrected pipeline: resolved identities on retained rows | `r sum(products$era & !products$carob)` | `r sum(products$era & products$carob)` | `r sum(!products$era & products$carob)` |

**678 was a count of labels, not new crops.** The June transform used `P.Product` before the later crop substitutions. The conservative comparison uses the bundled ERA master `prod` vocabulary: whole product, simple product or scientific name must resolve to one plant product. A small spelling/synonym list aligns labels such as *faba bean / fava bean*, *sweetpotato / sweet potato* and *lucerne / alfalfa*. Maize occurs in both; avocado is ERA-only and hazelnut Carob-only among resolved June products. A product is not necessarily a botanical species. “Only” means only among resolved observations in these two inputs.

The [label ledger](report/audit/crop_labels.csv) shows counts and decisions on both sides. Bamboo–maize is a compound, not another crop; variety names require parent crop context. Do not assign yield to the first member of a mixture or conflate rice bean with rice. Ambiguous and unknown labels stay unresolved. Missing crop accounts for `r fmt(s$era_missing)` ERA and `r fmt(s$carob_missing)` Carob rows in the historical replay. [Current product list](report/audit/current_products.csv) and [current label counts](report/audit/current_crop_labels.csv)

### Why the historical totals changed

The [June report](https://github.com/CGIAR-AgWise/era-carob/tree/81eef14c11437bddf8bb5914436e4525b45c6cce) recorded 244,094 ERA rows and 491,087 stacked rows across 321 columns. Replay gives **`r fmt(s$era_rows)` and `r fmt(s$merged)`**, respectively, with the same `r fmt(s$carob_rows)` Carob baseline, 1,720 ERA IDs and 17 ERA-only country strings. This run pins R collation to C. Under C.UTF-8 the same inputs produced 243,998 ERA rows (490,991 stacked). Row-order pairing makes counts sensitive to sort order; the original environment and the remaining 53-row difference are unverified; do not cite either historical total as new observations. The baseline has 320 fields before the source indicator.

The old full joins used all common column names as keys and included unmatched lookup records. Soil joined only on study and site, increasing 182,835 rows to 259,438 before filtering and reshaping. Then the outcome pivot paired observations by within-variable row number. [Stage-by-stage keys and counts](report/audit/historical_joins.csv). The corrected build starts with outcomes, attaches only unambiguous complete lookup keys, keeps the source ordinal through reshaping and flags unresolved crops. This sacrifices ambiguous attributes to preserve outcome identity. Review treatment, replication and unit assumptions before analysis.

### Reusing treatment means

Study AC0017 illustrates what the merged data can support. In Malawi, maize grain yield averaged 3,990 kg/ha under pit planting plus mulch and 1,840 kg/ha under farmer practice. The **2,150 kg/ha difference** agrees with the paper's table across nine seasons. Treat the pair as one study-period contrast. The reported replication count and arm errors alone cannot establish its sampling variance. For NN0421, the ERA figure extraction and the paper's results text disagree. Review that discrepancy before pooling the contrast. [Worked examples and primary sources](report/audit/meta_example.md)

The [crop crosswalk](report/audit/terminag_crop_crosswalk.csv) checks 161 retained crop labels against the [pinned Terminag crop table](https://github.com/controvoc/terminag/blob/31732136beeb34eda26f1874c2487beecef63cab/values/values_crop.csv). Of the 67 without an exact name, 4 are listed synonyms, 5 match through a scientific name, FAO name or spacing, and 9 map through the ERA plant master by scientific name. Tracing those remaining 49 labels to 2,419 original ERA outcome rows across 92 studies added nine crop matches and 14 broader groups. Eleven labels need Cedric’s source review and 15 have vocabulary gaps. NN0090 also needs a cultivar check after its crop was resolved as peach. See [review decisions](report/audit/crop_source_review.csv) and [study evidence with source-row locators](report/audit/crop_source_evidence.csv).

Use the [field dictionary](report/field_dictionary.xlsx) or its [CSV edition](report/field_dictionary.csv) for definitions, units, source coverage and study-specific exceptions. It compares the merged fields with [Terminag](https://github.com/controvoc/terminag) and links the contributing [Carob project](https://github.com/carob-data).

The [schema workbook](report/era_carob_mapping.xlsx) gives field sources and the number of populated rows. The candidate preserves ERA's original outcome, value, unit, uncertainty and harvest-part label beside harmonised fields. Soil carbon concentration and stock have different units. An irrigation method can establish irrigation use even when the water quantity is unknown. ERA's mean annual site rainfall has its own field because Carob defines rainfall over the crop season.

### Climate and model readiness

The table below is the **historical May 2025 input screen**, retained for reproducibility. It uses original ERA outcomes and Carob wide rows, before any climate join. Coordinate checks require a finite, in-range pair other than (0,0); dates require a valid day and a plausible planting year. For ERA we also require a unique recorded season year matching the planting year. A full season window, grid-cell match and observed weather are **not** established by this screen.

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
knitr::kable(qc,format="pipe",format.args=list(big.mark=","))
```

The current date-only successor yields **40,655 accepted ERA planting dates**, from 70,161 raw planting dates on 110,277 retained ERA rows. The existing same-year screen excludes 29,506 raw dates; 1,237 accepted-date rows lack coordinates. [Current date counts and exact input pins](report/audit/date_snapshot.json) supersede the historical date counts above. Eight accepted-date outcomes still have held harvest dates and fail the climate hold check. These totals do not measure climate coverage.

The consumer preserves source planting text, requires an exact day matching a single recorded season year, and rejects year 9999. The source release retains 900 unresolved row/field findings: no inferred century, year or missing day, and no automatic filling of held dates. Climate handoff checks reject held ERA outcome rows. See [date precision, provenance and holds](docs/SF-003.md#date-origin-precision-and-source-holds). No reviewed climate output is available in this repository; climate and model readiness remain unverified. Namita owns climate integration and source interpretation; Cedric reviews the transformation.
